title: SMP: A General Hyperedge-Based Framework for Circuit-Level Quantum Error Correction
authors: Siying Wang, Yue Yan, Zhixin Xia, Canwei Shi, Hannuo Yuan, Xiang-Bin Wang
abstract: Hyperedge faults remain a major challenge in circuit-level quantum error correction. Accurately exploiting hyperedge correlations often requires substantial computational resources, which complicates real-time decoding. Matching-based decoders are fast and scalable, but their pairwise graph representation limits the use of higher-order fault information. Here, we introduce Syndrome Motif Projection (SMP), a general framework for incorporating hyperedge information into matching-based decoding. The key idea is that a hyperedge fault produces a characteristic local syndrome motif. Observing such a motif provides evidence for the corresponding fault. SMP extracts this information directly from the measured syndrome with linear-complexity preprocessing while preserving the matching backend. It can therefore serve as a lightweight front end to existing scalable and real-time matching decoders. We demonstrate SMP across surface code memories, color code memories, and logical gate circuits. On Google's Willow experimental surface code data, SMP improves both standard and correlated matching and outperforms the tested belief matching baseline. For color code memories, SMP combined with Chromobius reduces logical failure probabilities by up to 77.8\%. For logical gate circuits, SMP reduces the failure probability of a six-CNOT circuit by 35.5\% relative to logical observable matching while achieving performance comparable to iterative belief matching. These results demonstrate that SMP provides a lightweight and transferable approach to hyperedge decoding, with a clear path toward integration into scalable real-time decoding architectures for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
summary: This paper introduces Syndrome Motif Projection (SMP), a novel, lightweight framework designed to incorporate complex hyperedge fault information into existing, scalable matching-based quantum error correction decoders. By extracting local syndrome motifs, SMP enhances the ability to detect and correct correlated errors in surface and color codes. The results demonstrate that SMP provides a highly transferable method to boost fault tolerance in real-time quantum computation architectures.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is accurately decoding hyperedge faults in circuit-level quantum error correction (QEC), as existing fast decoders are limited by pairwise representations.
main_result: The proposed Syndrome Motif Projection (SMP) framework significantly improves error correction performance across surface and color codes, achieving reductions in logical failure probabilities up to 77.8% and 35.5% compared to baselines.
method: SMP is a lightweight front-end that extracts characteristic local syndrome motifs directly from measured syndromes, allowing this higher-order fault information to be incorporated into existing, scalable matching-based decoding algorithms.
model_or_system: The work focuses on circuit-level QEC using stabilizer measurements on physical systems modeled by surface codes and color codes, aiming for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
key_observables: Logical failure probabilities ($P_L$), performance improvement over belief matching, and the detection of specific syndrome motifs.
important_parameters: Physical error probability ($p$), code distance ($d$), and the structure of the fault (edge vs. hyperedge).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the local syndrome motif provides sufficient evidence to effectively update the weights in the matching backend, allowing for a linear-complexity preprocessing step.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the structure of hyperedges and the resulting syndrome motifs from circuit-level faults in a surface code patch. Other figures compare the logical failure probabilities of various decoding methods.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the SMP framework by defining the problem of hyperedge faults, details the mechanism of motif extraction and weight interpolation ($\eta_h$), and validates the approach by demonstrating performance improvements across surface codes, color codes, and logical gate circuits.
why_interesting: While focused on QEC, the development of lightweight, information-theoretic preprocessing steps (like motif extraction) that bridge complex physical phenomena (hyperedge faults) into computationally tractable graph structures is relevant to designing efficient control protocols for open quantum systems.
